commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[Core] Shadow L1: index borrowed views of a peer's bytes without payload (#6207)

* [Core] Shadow L1: index borrowed views of a peer's bytes without payload

Let an L2 adapter lend a peer's KV bytes instead of copying them into
local L1. The read path only serves what an L1 indexes, so lending needs
an L1 that indexes bytes it does not own: a shadow L1.

- `LendingPeerL2AdapterBase(PeerL2AdapterBase)`: the abstract lender. It
  wants a `REMOTE` L1, carries the shadow L1 the storage manager creates
  for it (`bind_shadow_l1`) and closes it with itself.
- `BorrowedMemoryObj`: the lease contract a lender hands over (`lease`,
  `release`, `same_bytes` for lease adoption, `local_device` for the fence
  on close); `BorrowedTensorMemoryObj` is the view of locally mapped
  bytes. `ShadowL1Manager` indexes them and owns no memory; `admit`
  read-locks each view for one request, and a key already resident adopts
  the fresh lease when both views alias the same bytes. A shadow holds a
  disabled event bus, which now registers no gauges.
- `StorageManager` creates the shadow for a `REMOTE`-first config, refuses
  serde on a lender and a lender/config mismatch, and undoes a failed
  `add_l2_adapter`. `PrefetchController` looks the lender up on every
  prefetch, admits its views, unlocks the keys that did not become views,
  and holds a lender until its views drain.
- Independent fix: the copy-load path counts only `SUCCESS` admissions as
  hits.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: implement the L1 primitives; lenders go through the ordinary load pipeline

Review (ApostaC): let the shadow L1 implement reserve_write and the other
primitives so the prefetch controller needs no lender-specific path.

- `ShadowL1Manager.reserve_write` stages a `BorrowedMemoryObj` placeholder
  per key with no capacity check, always temporary; a key another request
  still reads is staged too. `finish_write_and_reserve_read` admits bound
  placeholders; a resident view adopts the fresh lease of the same bytes.
  `reserve_read` misses every key: every request borrows afresh. `admit`
  and `take_borrowed_objects` are gone.
- `BorrowedMemoryObj` is one concrete class: a placeholder the shadow's
  memory manager hands out, which the lender's `submit_load_task` binds to
  its lease and to the bytes (a tensor view, or `read_into` for remote
  bytes). `BorrowedTensorMemoryObj` is gone.
- The prefetch controller keeps only the lender's affinity (its shadow)
  and the NO_LOCK exclusion. The storage manager's `delete_l2_adapter`
  waits for the lender's borrowed views to drain, sweeping lapsed readers.
- `MemoryResidency.DUMMY` becomes `SHADOW`; shadows are tagged
  `(segment, SHADOW)` and a lender wants `SHADOW` first.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: a remote-bound BorrowedMemoryObj has no tensor, byte array or data pointer

The lending mock also unlocks through PeerL2AdapterBase directly, as its
lease release does, so a subclass between them can keep its own
reservations without the mock's unlocks going through them.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: shorter docstrings and docs; one L1-container rebuild per side; fold overlapping tests

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Docs] memory tags: drop the shadow sentence under the L1 tag table

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: admission refuses nothing; the copy-admission filter leaves this PR

A lease that ends between a lender's load and the admission is the same
race as one ending right after: the view is resident and unreadable, and
its holder's finish_read returns the lease. So the shadow's
finish_write_and_reserve_read only adopts a fresh lease into a resident
view and defers to the base, and `_poll_load_results` is back to dev. The
expired-write-reservation bug of owned L1s is unrelated and gets its own PR.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: a failed lender add only unlists its shadow

The general add_l2_adapter rollback leaves this PR: as on dev, an adapter
whose controller registration failed stays for delete_l2_adapter to
remove. What a lender needs is one guard: its shadow L1 is not listed when
nothing routes to it. Removal recognises a lender by type, so a
half-registered lender can be deleted.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: inline the single-call borrowed_segment into _build_l2_adapter

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: reword the SHADOW residency

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: one lends flag and one cleanup path in _build_l2_adapter

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: get_local_borrow_count, the count is this node's

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: BorrowingPeerL2AdapterBase; the owner lends, this adapter borrows

The adapter borrows a peer's bytes on behalf of this node; "lender" named
the wrong side. The mock and its registry names follow.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: reclaim expired placeholders; a remote binding needs the owner's address; one critical section per override

Review findings:
- A placeholder whose write reservation expired before admission stayed
  staged forever (a shadow has no eviction) and the base handed it, still
  bound, to the next writer. The shadow's sweep now reclaims expired
  staging entries too.
- `bind(read_into=...)` accepted the default address, so two remote views
  of different copies compared as the same bytes. The address is required.
- `reserve_write` and `finish_write_and_reserve_read` swapped leases and
  then re-entered the base under a second lock acquisition; a reader's
  `finish_read` in between could free the resident view. The shadow uses a
  reentrant lock so each override is one critical section.
Also: `for_borrower`, borrower names in the tests, no hard-coded memory
format on placeholders.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: restore the is_multi_l1 docstring

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: a configured L1, not one the borrower brings

The shadow L1 is configured like any other L1 (`--l1-manager '{"type":
"SHADOW", "tag": ..., "segment": ...}'`, `ShadowL1ManagerConfig`) and is
the affinity of the borrowing L2 adapters of its segment, resolved by
tags like every adapter's. It owns no memory, so an idle shadow costs
nothing; its store and eviction controllers are inert because a shadow
calls no listener. The storage manager no longer creates, attaches or
detaches a shadow per borrower; the prefetch controller skips an L1
without capacity at admission and keeps borrowers out of NO_LOCK by the
affinity L1's residency tag. `BorrowingPeerL2AdapterBase` loses
`shadow_l1` / `bind_shadow_l1`; removal still waits for a borrower's
views to be released. A shadow cannot be the first L1, which receives
the engine's writes.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: removal is the borrower's business, not the storage manager's

The storage manager and the P2P adapter base are back to dev. A
borrower's `close` refuses while a view holds a live lease, and
`delete_l2_adapter` keeps a failed close for a retry as it does for any
adapter; the shadow's public `sweep_lapsed` goes with the drain loop
(entries whose readers' TTL lapsed are swept at the next reservation).
`BorrowingPeerL2AdapterBase` leaves this PR: nothing here needs to tell a
borrower apart, since affinity, admission and NO_LOCK go by the shadow's
tags. The borrowing mock subclasses `PeerL2AdapterBase`.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Docs] Shadow L1: a shorter design section

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Tests] Shadow L1: type the borrowing test helpers for mypy

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Docs] Shadow L1: a shorter class docstring

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: same_bytes compares the owner as well as the address

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

commits.message:
[P2P] Add peer write RPCs and the P2P adapter store path (#6532)

* [P2P] Add peer write RPCs and the P2P adapter store path

Second part of P2P write support (after the transfer-channel writes in
#6401). A main server can now store KV objects into a peer's L1, which lets
a headless peer extend the main server's DRAM pool. Nothing is reachable
from the CLI yet: P2PL2AdapterConfig.write_enabled defaults to False.

- RPCs p2p_reserve_write and p2p_finish_write (RequestClient contract and
  gRPC proto).
- P2PController serves them statelessly through the L1 registered with
  the transfer channel, under the writer tag "p2p". An abandoned
  reservation expires with the L1 write TTL.
- P2PL2Adapter stores in three steps: reserve, RDMA write, commit. The
  reservation's done-callback starts the transfer, the commit's
  done-callback wakes the store loop, and neither store method waits on
  the peer. A task succeeds only when every key is resident on the peer.
- Design doc, unit tests, transport parity tests and real-NIXL
  integration tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: ApostaC <yihua@tensormesh.ai>

The tracked type stub now has the four messages added to

commits.message:
[Perf][MP] Keep prefetched keys in L1 under the default prefetch policy (#6428)

With the default store policy a key stays in L1 after its L2 store,
but with the default prefetch policy a key loaded back from L2 is
freed right after the read, so the next request loads it again.

The default prefetch policy now keeps loaded keys in L1. The old
behavior is a new policy named skip_l1, like the store policy that
uses L1 only as a buffer. "retain" now does the same as "default", so
it stays as a deprecated alias that logs a warning.

so loaded keys kept in L1 are never freed. The config logs a warning
for that setup unless the prefetch policy is skip_l1 too. Configs and
docs that pair --l2-store-policy skip_l1 with --l2-prefetch-policy
default now use skip_l1 for both, and the operator accepts skip_l1
for prefetchPolicy. Tests that check that loaded keys leave L1 set
the skip_l1 prefetch policy.

commits.author: Lin Sun
commits.message:
[MP][ROCm] Opt-in host-side wait for the engine's event (`--rocm-host-event-wait`) (#6212)

* [MP] Affinity pool: let a handler answer later with a DeferredResponse

A task may return a DeferredResponse (a concurrent.futures.Future) instead of
its result. The worker thread is then free for the next task, and the future
returned by AffinityThreadPool.submit() completes with the deferred
response's result or exception. Tasks returning anything else behave as
before.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

* [MP] --rocm-host-event-wait: opt-in host-side producer-event wait (ROCm workaround)

On MI3xx the command processor cannot keep an unsatisfied cross-queue
barrier resident: a stream wait on the engine's pending IPC event
(hipStreamWaitEvent on an imported event) is offloaded and reconnected on a
timer, and those wakeups slow the engine's kernels on the same hardware pipe
while the engine runs the step (about 30 % for prefill steps on MI355X).

New server flag --rocm-host-event-wait (default off; also
LMCACHE_ROCM_HOST_EVENT_WAIT=1). When it is set on ROCm, LMCache-driven
STORE / RETRIEVE enqueue their copies only once the producer event has
completed, checked with non-blocking query() calls:

- a transfer whose event has completed, with nothing queued ahead of it for
  the same instance, runs inline in the handler;
- otherwise it joins a per-instance FIFO drained by one poller thread
  (50 us backoff doubling to 1 ms) and the handler answers with a
  DeferredResponse, so the affinity thread that serves every rank is never
  blocked;
- a transfer still waiting after 60 s or at shutdown submits no device work
  and answers (b"", False); a waiting retrieve releases its lookup locks.

The store / retrieve bodies are unchanged: the waiter re-runs the same
handler, and inside that run the instance's event backend returns the event
it polled and skips the stream wait on it. Counters (inline, deferred,
timeout, shutdown, device_waits, pending) are reported in the module status.

Off (the default) on every platform, and on + not ROCm (one warning), no
waiter or thread is created and store / retrieve run the upstream code;
the only lines they execute that differ are the "waiter is None" checks.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

* [MP] --rocm-host-event-wait: poller only checks events, transfers run on the affinity worker

- The poller only checks events; a completed transfer is handed back to the
  affinity worker that received it (current_worker_poster). This keeps the
  affinity pool's existing design that all operations for an instance run on
  one thread (no locks on its shared temporary GPU buffer, ordered with the
  other affinity handlers such as CacheBlend), which running transfers on the
  poller thread broke.
- stop() vs the inline probe: the probe and inline run count as active work,
  _stopped is re-checked before running or enqueueing, and stop() fails every
  transfer not started yet and waits for the running ones.
- A waiting transfer runs only against the registration that supplied its
  event; otherwise the existing unregistered-instance path rejects it.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

* [MP] --rocm-host-event-wait: drop the lock release on a failed waiting RETRIEVE

After merging dev: dev now includes #6252, which removed
_release_failed_retrieve_locks. This PR's _fail_waiting_retrieve still
called it, so mypy failed (attr-defined). The tests in
test_rocm_host_event_wait.py failed too: their setup replaced the removed
method with a function that only records the request ID, and that
replacement fails once the method no longer exists.

Changes:
- Remove _fail_waiting_retrieve. A RETRIEVE whose producer-event wait
  timed out or was stopped now answers (b"", False) without releasing
  locks, like #6252's rejection path: the unconsumed lookup read-lock
  share expires with the L1 read-lock TTL.
- Tests: remove that replacement and the three assertions that checked
  its recorded request IDs; rename
  test_timeout_fails_store_and_releases_retrieve_locks to
  test_timeout_fails_store_and_retrieve.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

* [MP] --rocm-host-event-wait: close the remaining registration and shutdown gaps

1. A STORE / RETRIEVE for an instance that is not registered is rejected
   right away.

   An engine worker registers its KV cache once (REGISTER_KV_CACHE): the
   server maps the worker's KV memory and keeps a ContextEntry under the
   worker's instance ID. STORE / RETRIEVE look that entry up by instance
   ID. There is none when the worker sends a transfer before it has
   registered with this server (e.g. after a server restart), or after
   it was unregistered or reaped for being silent.

   Without this option the handler looks the instance up once and, if
   there is no entry, answers (b"", False) without any device work. With
   the option, submit_after_event instead ran the handler again, which
   looked the instance up a second time. REGISTER runs on the MQ main
   loop, not on the affinity worker, so the instance could be registered
   between the two lookups, and the request then ran against a
   registration it was not sent to, waiting on its event on the device.
   Now, when that one lookup finds no entry, the waiter returns
   (b"", False) directly and does not call the handler: no second
   lookup, no event import, no device work, the same answer as without
   the option.

2. A waiting transfer keeps only a weak reference to its registration.

   A weak reference (weakref.ref) does not keep the entry alive: once
   the registry and the release path drop the entry, it is freed and the
   reference returns None. Unregistering or reaping an instance passes
   the entry to _release_entries, which relies on holding the last
   reference: with the default CudaIPCWrapper, ipc_collect() unmaps the
   worker's KV memory only after the last tensor reference is gone. A
   waiting transfer held the entry, so the memory of an unregistered or
   reaped worker stayed mapped while the transfer waited (up to the 60 s
   event timeout), after _release_entries had already run ipc_collect().
   Now the entry is freed when it is released, and the waiting transfer
   is rejected as stale ((b"", False)) when its event completes.

3. stop() handles only the waiter's own queue and poller.

   close() (server shutdown) calls stop() before it releases the cache
   contexts. The server's shutdown does not wait for its handlers: the
   transport shuts the affinity pool down with wait=False, and then
   engine.close() closes the modules. stop() instead also failed the
   transfers it had handed to an affinity worker, and waited up to 10 s
   for the running ones before it returned anyway. Now stop() fails only
   the transfers still waiting for their event in its queue, which the
   stopped poller would never run, and stops the poller. A transfer
   already handed to its affinity worker, or running, is left to that
   worker, as without the option; so is an inline transfer whose event
   has completed. The 60 s timeout for a producer event that never
   completes is unchanged.

Tests: a registration made right after a missing-entry lookup is not
used (STORE and RETRIEVE); a re-registration before an inline run drops
the transfer; unregistering frees the entry of a waiting transfer (STORE
and RETRIEVE); stop() neither waits for a running transfer nor fails one
handed to its worker; after stop(), an inline transfer runs if its event
completed and fails if not.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

* [MP] --rocm-host-event-wait: stop() fails hand-offs that have not started

The server shuts down in two steps: server.close() queues the affinity
pool's shutdown sentinel, then engine.close() closes the modules, which
stops the waiter. The poller still runs until stop(): a transfer whose
event completes in between is handed to its affinity worker behind the
sentinel, the worker exits first, and the transfer's response was never
settled.

The poller now records a hand-off until the worker starts it, and stop()
fails the hand-offs that have not started along with the transfers still
waiting for their event. Whichever of the worker and stop() takes a
hand-off first settles it. A running transfer is still left to its
worker.

Tests: a hand-off queued after the worker shutdown sentinel is failed by
stop(); so is one queued behind a busy worker.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

commits.author: sssqqeer
commits.message:
[Perf][MP] Dispatch fs_native lookups and reads straight to the read pool (#6670)

Even with the 256-thread read pool enabled, FSConnector still routed
submit_batch_exists and submit_batch_get through ConnectorBase's shared
4-worker queue, and each pooled GET held a shared worker until its tile
finished. A background store of four or more chunks filled all four
workers in write_all + rename, stalling foreground lookups and reads
while the reader threads sat idle, and small GET batches could keep at
most num_workers batches in flight across the pool.

When the read pool is active, enqueue exists and get batches directly on
the pool and have the reader finishing the last key emit the completion.
Lookups drain ahead of reads without charging the read byte budget, and
reads pop one object at a time as the budget allows.

Signed-off-by: shibin <306219114@qq.com>

commits.author: Daegyu Han
commits.message:
[Bugfix][MP] Stage prefetch keys that land in L1 during the L2 lookup (#6392)

* [Bugfix][MP] Stage prefetch keys that land in L1 during the L2 lookup

A key another request's load admits to L1 between this request's L1
lock pass and its reserve_write made the reservation fail with
KEY_NOT_WRITABLE. The cell was reported as l1_contended, and under the
prefix policy the hit stopped before it, turning a resident chunk into a
miss that the engine recomputed.

reserve_write gains allow_resident: when set, a key that is already
resident is staged like any other. Admission already handles that case
(finish_write_and_reserve_read discards the staging buffer and read-locks
the resident object), so the prefetch controller's state machine is
unchanged. The controller passes the flag only for an L1 the request may
read: the lock pass covers only those, so a resident key there landed
during the lookup. In an affinity L1 excluded by allowed_l1_memory_tags a
resident key stays a miss, as before, and is what l1_contended now
reports. The cost is one redundant L2 load of the landed key, which two
overlapping loads already pay when both reserve before either lands.
Other writers keep the default, so engine stores still de-duplicate on
KEY_NOT_WRITABLE. ShadowL1Manager already stages resident keys.

The two tests that pinned the old drop now expect every key served under
both the prefix and full policies, and fail without the controller
change. An L1 interface test covers the flag and the admission of a
resident key. Docs, the metric description and the P2P skill references
now describe l1_contended by its new meaning.

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <hdg9400@gmail.com>

* [Bugfix][MP] Address review: keyword-only allow_resident, document the remaining misses

- allow_resident is keyword-only on L1ManagerInterface, BaseL1Manager
  and ShadowL1Manager, so call sites read as intended.
- staging-and-write-tags.md: a landed key is still a miss when the second
  buffer cannot be allocated (l1_oom) or the redundant load fails.
- prefetch_controller.md: the NO_LOCK limitation (a request can be served
  a temporary resident object that is freed when its last reader releases
  it) moves from the PR description into the limitations list, and the
  TestReservationFailures bullet now says a key landed after the lock pass

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[Core] Shadow L1: index borrowed views of a peer's bytes without payload (#6207)

* [Core] Shadow L1: index borrowed views of a peer's bytes without payload

Let an L2 adapter lend a peer's KV bytes instead of copying them into
local L1. The read path only serves what an L1 indexes, so lending needs
an L1 that indexes bytes it does not own: a shadow L1.

- `LendingPeerL2AdapterBase(PeerL2AdapterBase)`: the abstract lender. It
  wants a `REMOTE` L1, carries the shadow L1 the storage manager creates
  for it (`bind_shadow_l1`) and closes it with itself.
- `BorrowedMemoryObj`: the lease contract a lender hands over (`lease`,
  `release`, `same_bytes` for lease adoption, `local_device` for the fence
  on close); `BorrowedTensorMemoryObj` is the view of locally mapped
  bytes. `ShadowL1Manager` indexes them and owns no memory; `admit`
  read-locks each view for one request, and a key already resident adopts
  the fresh lease when both views alias the same bytes. A shadow holds a
  disabled event bus, which now registers no gauges.
- `StorageManager` creates the shadow for a `REMOTE`-first config, refuses
  serde on a lender and a lender/config mismatch, and undoes a failed
  `add_l2_adapter`. `PrefetchController` looks the lender up on every
  prefetch, admits its views, unlocks the keys that did not become views,
  and holds a lender until its views drain.
- Independent fix: the copy-load path counts only `SUCCESS` admissions as
  hits.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: implement the L1 primitives; lenders go through the ordinary load pipeline

Review (ApostaC): let the shadow L1 implement reserve_write and the other
primitives so the prefetch controller needs no lender-specific path.

- `ShadowL1Manager.reserve_write` stages a `BorrowedMemoryObj` placeholder
  per key with no capacity check, always temporary; a key another request
  still reads is staged too. `finish_write_and_reserve_read` admits bound
  placeholders; a resident view adopts the fresh lease of the same bytes.
  `reserve_read` misses every key: every request borrows afresh. `admit`
  and `take_borrowed_objects` are gone.
- `BorrowedMemoryObj` is one concrete class: a placeholder the shadow's
  memory manager hands out, which the lender's `submit_load_task` binds to
  its lease and to the bytes (a tensor view, or `read_into` for remote
  bytes). `BorrowedTensorMemoryObj` is gone.
- The prefetch controller keeps only the lender's affinity (its shadow)
  and the NO_LOCK exclusion. The storage manager's `delete_l2_adapter`
  waits for the lender's borrowed views to drain, sweeping lapsed readers.
- `MemoryResidency.DUMMY` becomes `SHADOW`; shadows are tagged
  `(segment, SHADOW)` and a lender wants `SHADOW` first.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: a remote-bound BorrowedMemoryObj has no tensor, byte array or data pointer

The lending mock also unlocks through PeerL2AdapterBase directly, as its
lease release does, so a subclass between them can keep its own

* [P2P] Add peer write RPCs and the P2P adapter store path

Second part of P2P write support (after the transfer-channel writes in
#6401). A main server can now store KV objects into a peer's L1, which lets
a headless peer extend the main server's DRAM pool. Nothing is reachable
from the CLI yet: P2PL2AdapterConfig.write_enabled defaults to False.

- RPCs p2p_reserve_write and p2p_finish_write (RequestClient contract and
  gRPC proto).
- P2PController serves them statelessly through the L1 registered with
  the transfer channel, under the writer tag "p2p". An abandoned
  reservation expires with the L1 write TTL.
- P2PL2Adapter stores in three steps: reserve, RDMA write, commit. The
  reservation's done-callback starts the transfer, the commit's
  done-callback wakes the store loop, and neither store method waits on
  the peer. A task succeeds only when every key is resident on the peer.
- Design doc, unit tests, transport parity tests and real-NIXL
  integration tests.

commits.author: sssqqeer
commits.message:
[Perf][MP] Keep prefetched keys in L1 under the default prefetch policy (#6428)

With the default store policy a key stays in L1 after its L2 store,
but with the default prefetch policy a key loaded back from L2 is
freed right after the read, so the next request loads it again.

The default prefetch policy now keeps loaded keys in L1. The old
behavior is a new policy named skip_l1, like the store policy that
uses L1 only as a buffer. "retain" now does the same as "default", so
it stays as a deprecated alias that logs a warning.

Buffer-only mode pairs the skip_l1 store policy with noop eviction,
so loaded keys kept in L1 are never freed. The config logs a warning
for that setup unless the prefetch policy is skip_l1 too. Configs and

commits.author: Lin Sun
commits.message:
[MP][ROCm] Opt-in host-side wait for the engine's event (`--rocm-host-event-wait`) (#6212)

* [MP] Affinity pool: let a handler answer later with a DeferredResponse

A task may return a DeferredResponse (a concurrent.futures.Future) instead of
its result. The worker thread is then free for the next task, and the future
returned by AffinityThreadPool.submit() completes with the deferred
response's result or exception. Tasks returning anything else behave as
before.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

* [MP] --rocm-host-event-wait: opt-in host-side producer-event wait (ROCm workaround)

On MI3xx the command processor cannot keep an unsatisfied cross-queue
barrier resident: a stream wait on the engine's pending IPC event
(hipStreamWaitEvent on an imported event) is offloaded and reconnected on a
timer, and those wakeups slow the engine's kernels on the same hardware pipe
while the engine runs the step (about 30 % for prefill steps on MI355X).

New server flag --rocm-host-event-wait (default off; also
LMCACHE_ROCM_HOST_EVENT_WAIT=1). When it is set on ROCm, LMCache-driven
STORE / RETRIEVE enqueue their copies only once the producer event has
completed, checked with non-blocking query() calls:

- a transfer whose event has completed, with nothing queued ahead of it for
  the same instance, runs inline in the handler;
- otherwise it joins a per-instance FIFO drained by one poller thread
  (50 us backoff doubling to 1 ms) and the handler answers with a
  DeferredResponse, so the affinity thread that serves every rank is never
  blocked;
- a transfer still waiting after 60 s or at shutdown submits no device work
  and answers (b"", False); a waiting retrieve releases its lookup locks.

The store / retrieve bodies are unchanged: the waiter re-runs the same
handler, and inside that run the instance's event backend returns the event
it polled and skips the stream wait on it. Counters (inline, deferred,
timeout, shutdown, device_waits, pending) are reported in the module status.

Off (the default) on every platform, and on + not ROCm (one warning), no
waiter or thread is created and store / retrieve run the upstream code;
the only lines they execute that differ are the "waiter is None" checks.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

* [MP] --rocm-host-event-wait: poller only checks events, transfers run on the affinity worker

- The poller only checks events; a completed transfer is handed back to the
  affinity worker that received it (current_worker_poster). This keeps the
  affinity pool's existing design that all operations for an instance run on
  one thread (no locks on its shared temporary GPU buffer, ordered with the
  other affinity handlers such as CacheBlend), which running transfers on the
  poller thread broke.
- stop() vs the inline probe: the probe and inline run count as active work,
  _stopped is re-checked before running or enqueueing, and stop() fails every
  transfer not started yet and waits for the running ones.
- A waiting transfer runs only against the registration that supplied its
  event; otherwise the existing unregistered-instance path rejects it.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

* [MP] --rocm-host-event-wait: drop the lock release on a failed waiting RETRIEVE

After merging dev: dev now includes #6252, which removed
_release_failed_retrieve_locks. This PR's _fail_waiting_retrieve still
called it, so mypy failed (attr-defined). The tests in
test_rocm_host_event_wait.py failed too: their setup replaced the removed
method with a function that only records the request ID, and that
replacement fails once the method no longer exists.

Changes:
- Remove _fail_waiting_retrieve. A RETRIEVE whose producer-event wait
  timed out or was stopped now answers (b"", False) without releasing
  locks, like #6252's rejection path: the unconsumed lookup read-lock
  share expires with the L1 read-lock TTL.
- Tests: remove that replacement and the three assertions that checked
  its recorded request IDs; rename
  test_timeout_fails_store_and_releases_retrieve_locks to
  test_timeout_fails_store_and_retrieve.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

* [MP] --rocm-host-event-wait: close the remaining registration and shutdown gaps

1. A STORE / RETRIEVE for an instance that is not registered is rejected
   right away.

   An engine worker registers its KV cache once (REGISTER_KV_CACHE): the
   server maps the worker's KV memory and keeps a ContextEntry under the
   worker's instance ID. STORE / RETRIEVE look that entry up by instance
   ID. There is none when the worker sends a transfer before it has
   registered with this server (e.g. after a server restart), or after
   it was unregistered or reaped for being silent.

   Without this option the handler looks the instance up once and, if
   there is no entry, answers (b"", False) without any device work. With
   the option, submit_after_event instead ran the handler again, which
   looked the instance up a second time. REGISTER runs on the MQ main
   loop, not on the affinity worker, so the instance could be registered
   between the two lookups, and the request then ran against a
   registration it was not sent to, waiting on its event on the device.
   Now, when that one lookup finds no entry, the waiter returns
   (b"", False) directly and does not call the handler: no second
   lookup, no event import, no device work, the same answer as without
   the option.

2. A waiting transfer keeps only a weak reference to its registration.

   A weak reference (weakref.ref) does not keep the entry alive: once
   the registry and the release path drop the entry, it is freed and the
   reference returns None. Unregistering or reaping an instance passes
   the entry to _release_entries, which relies on holding the last
   reference: with the default CudaIPCWrapper, ipc_collect() unmaps the
   worker's KV memory only after the last tensor reference is gone. A
   waiting transfer held the entry, so the memory of an unregistered or
   reaped worker stayed mapped while the transfer waited (up to the 60 s
   event timeout), after _release_entries had already run ipc_collect().
   Now the entry is freed when it is released, and the waiting transfer
   is rejected as stale ((b"", False)) when its event completes.

3. stop() handles only the waiter's own queue and poller.

   close() (server shutdown) calls stop() before it releases the cache
   contexts. The server's shutdown does not wait for its handlers: the
   transport shuts the affinity pool down with wait=False, and then
   engine.close() closes the modules. stop() instead also failed the
   transfers it had handed to an affinity worker, and waited up to 10 s
   for the running ones before it returned anyway. Now stop() fails only
   the transfers still waiting for their event in its queue, which the
   stopped poller would never run, and stops the poller. A transfer
   already handed to its affinity worker, or running, is left to that
   worker, as without the option; so is an inline transfer whose event
   has completed. The 60 s timeout for a producer event that never
   completes is unchanged.

Tests: a registration made right after a missing-entry lookup is not
used (STORE and RETRIEVE); a re-registration before an inline run drops
the transfer; unregistering frees the entry of a waiting transfer (STORE
and RETRIEVE); stop() neither waits for a running transfer nor fails one
handed to its worker; after stop(), an inline transfer runs if its event
completed and fails if not.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

* [MP] --rocm-host-event-wait: stop() fails hand-offs that have not started

The server shuts down in two steps: server.close() queues the affinity
pool's shutdown sentinel, then engine.close() closes the modules, which
stops the waiter. The poller still runs until stop(): a transfer whose
event completes in between is handed to its affinity worker behind the
sentinel, the worker exits first, and the transfer's response was never
settled.

The poller now records a hand-off until the worker starts it, and stop()
fails the hand-offs that have not started along with the transfers still
waiting for their event. Whichever of the worker and stop() takes a
hand-off first settles it. A running transfer is still left to its
worker.

Tests: a hand-off queued after the worker shutdown sentinel is failed by
stop(); so is one queued behind a busy worker.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

commits.author: Daegyu Han
commits.message:
[Bugfix][MP] Stage prefetch keys that land in L1 during the L2 lookup (#6392)

* [Bugfix][MP] Stage prefetch keys that land in L1 during the L2 lookup

A key another request's load admits to L1 between this request's L1
lock pass and its reserve_write made the reservation fail with
KEY_NOT_WRITABLE. The cell was reported as l1_contended, and under the
prefix policy the hit stopped before it, turning a resident chunk into a
miss that the engine recomputed.

reserve_write gains allow_resident: when set, a key that is already
resident is staged like any other. Admission already handles that case
(finish_write_and_reserve_read discards the staging buffer and read-locks
the resident object), so the prefetch controller's state machine is
unchanged. The controller passes the flag only for an L1 the request may
read: the lock pass covers only those, so a resident key there landed
during the lookup. In an affinity L1 excluded by allowed_l1_memory_tags a
resident key stays a miss, as before, and is what l1_contended now
reports. The cost is one redundant L2 load of the landed key, which two
overlapping loads already pay when both reserve before either lands.
Other writers keep the default, so engine stores still de-duplicate on
KEY_NOT_WRITABLE. ShadowL1Manager already stages resident keys.

The two tests that pinned the old drop now expect every key served under
both the prefix and full policies, and fail without the controller
change. An L1 interface test covers the flag and the admission of a
resident key. Docs, the metric description and the P2P skill references
now describe l1_contended by its new meaning.

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <hdg9400@gmail.com>

* [Bugfix][MP] Address review: keyword-only allow_resident, document the remaining misses

- allow_resident is keyword-only on L1ManagerInterface, BaseL1Manager
  and ShadowL1Manager, so call sites read as intended.
- staging-and-write-tags.md: a landed key is still a miss when the second
  buffer cannot be allocated (l1_oom) or the redundant load fails.
- prefetch_controller.md: the NO_LOCK limitation (a request can be served
  a temporary resident object that is freed when its last reader releases
  it) moves from the PR description into the limitations list, and the

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[Core] Shadow L1: index borrowed views of a peer's bytes without payload (#6207)

* [Core] Shadow L1: index borrowed views of a peer's bytes without payload

Let an L2 adapter lend a peer's KV bytes instead of copying them into
local L1. The read path only serves what an L1 indexes, so lending needs
an L1 that indexes bytes it does not own: a shadow L1.

- `LendingPeerL2AdapterBase(PeerL2AdapterBase)`: the abstract lender. It
  wants a `REMOTE` L1, carries the shadow L1 the storage manager creates
  for it (`bind_shadow_l1`) and closes it with itself.
- `BorrowedMemoryObj`: the lease contract a lender hands over (`lease`,
  `release`, `same_bytes` for lease adoption, `local_device` for the fence
  on close); `BorrowedTensorMemoryObj` is the view of locally mapped
  bytes. `ShadowL1Manager` indexes them and owns no memory; `admit`
  read-locks each view for one request, and a key already resident adopts
  the fresh lease when both views alias the same bytes. A shadow holds a
  disabled event bus, which now registers no gauges.
- `StorageManager` creates the shadow for a `REMOTE`-first config, refuses
  serde on a lender and a lender/config mismatch, and undoes a failed
  `add_l2_adapter`. `PrefetchController` looks the lender up on every
  prefetch, admits its views, unlocks the keys that did not become views,
  and holds a lender until its views drain.
- Independent fix: the copy-load path counts only `SUCCESS` admissions as
  hits.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: implement the L1 primitives; lenders go through the ordinary load pipeline

Review (ApostaC): let the shadow L1 implement reserve_write and the other
primitives so the prefetch controller needs no lender-specific path.

- `ShadowL1Manager.reserve_write` stages a `BorrowedMemoryObj` placeholder
  per key with no capacity check, always temporary; a key another request
  still reads is staged too. `finish_write_and_reserve_read` admits bound
  placeholders; a resident view adopts the fresh lease of the same bytes.
  `reserve_read` misses every key: every request borrows afresh. `admit`
  and `take_borrowed_objects` are gone.
- `BorrowedMemoryObj` is one concrete class: a placeholder the shadow's
  memory manager hands out, which the lender's `submit_load_task` binds to
  its lease and to the bytes (a tensor view, or `read_into` for remote
  bytes). `BorrowedTensorMemoryObj` is gone.
- The prefetch controller keeps only the lender's affinity (its shadow)
  and the NO_LOCK exclusion. The storage manager's `delete_l2_adapter`
  waits for the lender's borrowed views to drain, sweeping lapsed readers.
- `MemoryResidency.DUMMY` becomes `SHADOW`; shadows are tagged
  `(segment, SHADOW)` and a lender wants `SHADOW` first.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: a remote-bound BorrowedMemoryObj has no tensor, byte array or data pointer

The lending mock also unlocks through PeerL2AdapterBase directly, as its
lease release does, so a subclass between them can keep its own
reservations without the mock's unlocks going through them.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: shorter docstrings and docs; one L1-container rebuild per side; fold overlapping tests

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Docs] memory tags: drop the shadow sentence under the L1 tag table

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: admission refuses nothing; the copy-admission filter leaves this PR

A lease that ends between a lender's load and the admission is the same
race as one ending right after: the view is resident and unreadable, and
its holder's finish_read returns the lease. So the shadow's
finish_write_and_reserve_read only adopts a fresh lease into a resident
view and defers to the base, and `_poll_load_results` is back to dev. The
expired-write-reservation bug of owned L1s is unrelated and gets its own PR.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: a failed lender add only unlists its shadow

The general add_l2_adapter rollback leaves this PR: as on dev, an adapter
whose controller registration failed stays for delete_l2_adapter to
remove. What a lender needs is one guard: its shadow L1 is not listed when
nothing routes to it. Removal recognises a lender by type, so a
half-registered lender can be deleted.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: inline the single-call borrowed_segment into _build_l2_adapter

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: reword the SHADOW residency

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: one lends flag and one cleanup path in _build_l2_adapter

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: get_local_borrow_count, the count is this node's

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: BorrowingPeerL2AdapterBase; the owner lends, this adapter borrows

The adapter borrows a peer's bytes on behalf of this node; "lender" named
the wrong side. The mock and its registry names follow.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: reclaim expired placeholders; a remote binding needs the owner's address; one critical section per override

Review findings:
- A placeholder whose write reservation expired before admission stayed
  staged forever (a shadow has no eviction) and the base handed it, still
  bound, to the next writer. The shadow's sweep now reclaims expired
  staging entries too.
- `bind(read_into=...)` accepted the default address, so two remote views
  of different copies compared as the same bytes. The address is required.
- `reserve_write` and `finish_write_and_reserve_read` swapped leases and
  then re-entered the base under a second lock acquisition; a reader's
  `finish_read` in between could free the resident view. The shadow uses a
  reentrant lock so each override is one critical section.
Also: `for_borrower`, borrower names in the tests, no hard-coded memory
format on placeholders.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: restore the is_multi_l1 docstring

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: a configured L1, not one the borrower brings

The shadow L1 is configured like any other L1 (`--l1-manager '{"type":
"SHADOW", "tag": ..., "segment": ...}'`, `ShadowL1ManagerConfig`) and is
the affinity of the borrowing L2 adapters of its segment, resolved by
tags like every adapter's. It owns no memory, so an idle shadow costs
nothing; its store and eviction controllers are inert because a shadow
calls no listener. The storage manager no longer creates, attaches or
detaches a shadow per borrower; the prefetch controller skips an L1
without capacity at admission and keeps borrowers out of NO_LOCK by the
affinity L1's residency tag. `BorrowingPeerL2AdapterBase` loses
`shadow_l1` / `bind_shadow_l1`; removal still waits for a borrower's
views to be released. A shadow cannot be the first L1, which receives
the engine's writes.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: removal is the borrower's business, not the storage manager's

The storage manager and the P2P adapter base are back to dev. A
borrower's `close` refuses while a view holds a live lease, and
`delete_l2_adapter` keeps a failed close for a retry as it does for any
adapter; the shadow's public `sweep_lapsed` goes with the drain loop
(entries whose readers' TTL lapsed are swept at the next reservation).
`BorrowingPeerL2AdapterBase` leaves this PR: nothing here needs to tell a
borrower apart, since affinity, admission and NO_LOCK go by the shadow's
tags. The borrowing mock subclasses `PeerL2AdapterBase`.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Docs] Shadow L1: a shorter design section

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Tests] Shadow L1: type the borrowing test helpers for mypy

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Docs] Shadow L1: a shorter class docstring

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

* [Core] Shadow L1: same_bytes compares the owner as well as the address

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

commits.message:
[P2P] Add peer write RPCs and the P2P adapter store path (#6532)

* [P2P] Add peer write RPCs and the P2P adapter store path

Second part of P2P write support (after the transfer-channel writes in
#6401). A main server can now store KV objects into a peer's L1, which lets
a headless peer extend the main server's DRAM pool. Nothing is reachable
from the CLI yet: P2PL2AdapterConfig.write_enabled defaults to False.

  gRPC proto).
- P2PController serves them statelessly through the L1 registered with
  the transfer channel, under the writer tag "p2p". An abandoned
  reservation expires with the L1 write TTL.
- P2PL2Adapter stores in three steps: reserve, RDMA write, commit. The
  reservation's done-callback starts the transfer, the commit's
  done-callback wakes the store loop, and neither store method waits on
  the peer. A task succeeds only when every key is resident on the peer.
- Design doc, unit tests, transport parity tests and real-NIXL
  integration tests.

commits.author: sssqqeer
commits.message:
[Perf][MP] Keep prefetched keys in L1 under the default prefetch policy (#6428)

With the default store policy a key stays in L1 after its L2 store,
but with the default prefetch policy a key loaded back from L2 is
freed right after the read, so the next request loads it again.

The default prefetch policy now keeps loaded keys in L1. The old
behavior is a new policy named skip_l1, like the store policy that
uses L1 only as a buffer. "retain" now does the same as "default", so
it stays as a deprecated alias that logs a warning.

Buffer-only mode pairs the skip_l1 store policy with noop eviction,
so loaded keys kept in L1 are never freed. The config logs a warning
for that setup unless the prefetch policy is skip_l1 too. Configs and
docs that pair --l2-store-policy skip_l1 with --l2-prefetch-policy
default now use skip_l1 for both, and the operator accepts skip_l1
for prefetchPolicy. Tests that check that loaded keys leave L1 set
the skip_l1 prefetch policy.

Signed-off-by: shibin <306219114@qq.com>

commits.author: sssqqeer
commits.message:
[Perf][MP] Dispatch fs_native lookups and reads straight to the read pool (#6670)

Even with the 256-thread read pool enabled, FSConnector still routed
submit_batch_exists and submit_batch_get through ConnectorBase's shared
4-worker queue, and each pooled GET held a shared worker until its tile
finished. A background store of four or more chunks filled all four
workers in write_all + rename, stalling foreground lookups and reads
while the reader threads sat idle, and small GET batches could keep at
most num_workers batches in flight across the pool.

When the read pool is active, enqueue exists and get batches directly on
the pool and have the reader finishing the last key emit the completion.
Lookups drain ahead of reads without charging the read byte budget, and
reads pop one object at a time as the budget allows.

Signed-off-by: shibin <306219114@qq.com>

commits.author: Lin Sun
commits.message:
[MP][ROCm] Opt-in host-side wait for the engine's event (`--rocm-host-event-wait`) (#6212)

* [MP] Affinity pool: let a handler answer later with a DeferredResponse

A task may return a DeferredResponse (a concurrent.futures.Future) instead of
its result. The worker thread is then free for the next task, and the future
returned by AffinityThreadPool.submit() completes with the deferred
response's result or exception. Tasks returning anything else behave as
before.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

* [MP] --rocm-host-event-wait: opt-in host-side producer-event wait (ROCm workaround)

On MI3xx the command processor cannot keep an unsatisfied cross-queue
barrier resident: a stream wait on the engine's pending IPC event
(hipStreamWaitEvent on an imported event) is offloaded and reconnected on a
timer, and those wakeups slow the engine's kernels on the same hardware pipe
while the engine runs the step (about 30 % for prefill steps on MI355X).

New server flag --rocm-host-event-wait (default off; also
LMCACHE_ROCM_HOST_EVENT_WAIT=1). When it is set on ROCm, LMCache-driven
STORE / RETRIEVE enqueue their copies only once the producer event has
completed, checked with non-blocking query() calls:

- a transfer whose event has completed, with nothing queued ahead of it for
  the same instance, runs inline in the handler;
- otherwise it joins a per-instance FIFO drained by one poller thread
  (50 us backoff doubling to 1 ms) and the handler answers with a
  DeferredResponse, so the affinity thread that serves every rank is never
  blocked;
- a transfer still waiting after 60 s or at shutdown submits no device work
  and answers (b"", False); a waiting retrieve releases its lookup locks.

The store / retrieve bodies are unchanged: the waiter re-runs the same
handler, and inside that run the instance's event backend returns the event
it polled and skips the stream wait on it. Counters (inline, deferred,
timeout, shutdown, device_waits, pending) are reported in the module status.

Off (the default) on every platform, and on + not ROCm (one warning), no
waiter or thread is created and store / retrieve run the upstream code;
the only lines they execute that differ are the "waiter is None" checks.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

* [MP] --rocm-host-event-wait: poller only checks events, transfers run on the affinity worker

- The poller only checks events; a completed transfer is handed back to the
  affinity worker that received it (current_worker_poster). This keeps the
  affinity pool's existing design that all operations for an instance run on
  one thread (no locks on its shared temporary GPU buffer, ordered with the
  other affinity handlers such as CacheBlend), which running transfers on the
  poller thread broke.
- stop() vs the inline probe: the probe and inline run count as active work,
  _stopped is re-checked before running or enqueueing, and stop() fails every
  transfer not started yet and waits for the running ones.
- A waiting transfer runs only against the registration that supplied its
  event; otherwise the existing unregistered-instance path rejects it.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

* [MP] --rocm-host-event-wait: drop the lock release on a failed waiting RETRIEVE

After merging dev: dev now includes #6252, which removed
_release_failed_retrieve_locks. This PR's _fail_waiting_retrieve still
called it, so mypy failed (attr-defined). The tests in
test_rocm_host_event_wait.py failed too: their setup replaced the removed
method with a function that only records the request ID, and that
replacement fails once the method no longer exists.

Changes:
- Remove _fail_waiting_retrieve. A RETRIEVE whose producer-event wait
  timed out or was stopped now answers (b"", False) without releasing
  locks, like #6252's rejection path: the unconsumed lookup read-lock
  share expires with the L1 read-lock TTL.
- Tests: remove that replacement and the three assertions that checked
  its recorded request IDs; rename
  test_timeout_fails_store_and_releases_retrieve_locks to
  test_timeout_fails_store_and_retrieve.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

* [MP] --rocm-host-event-wait: close the remaining registration and shutdown gaps

1. A STORE / RETRIEVE for an instance that is not registered is rejected
   right away.

   An engine worker registers its KV cache once (REGISTER_KV_CACHE): the
   server maps the worker's KV memory and keeps a ContextEntry under the
   worker's instance ID. STORE / RETRIEVE look that entry up by instance
   ID. There is none when the worker sends a transfer before it has
   registered with this server (e.g. after a server restart), or after
   it was unregistered or reaped for being silent.

   Without this option the handler looks the instance up once and, if
   there is no entry, answers (b"", False) without any device work. With
   the option, submit_after_event instead ran the handler again, which
   looked the instance up a second time. REGISTER runs on the MQ main
   loop, not on the affinity worker, so the instance could be registered
   between the two lookups, and the request then ran against a
   registration it was not sent to, waiting on its event on the device.
   Now, when that one lookup finds no entry, the waiter returns
   (b"", False) directly and does not call the handler: no second
   lookup, no event import, no device work, the same answer as without
   the option.

2. A waiting transfer keeps only a weak reference to its registration.

   A weak reference (weakref.ref) does not keep the entry alive: once
   the registry and the release path drop the entry, it is freed and the
   reference returns None. Unregistering or reaping an instance passes
   the entry to _release_entries, which relies on holding the last
   reference: with the default CudaIPCWrapper, ipc_collect() unmaps the
   worker's KV memory only after the last tensor reference is gone. A
   waiting transfer held the entry, so the memory of an unregistered or
   reaped worker stayed mapped while the transfer waited (up to the 60 s
   event timeout), after _release_entries had already run ipc_collect().
   Now the entry is freed when it is released, and the waiting transfer
   is rejected as stale ((b"", False)) when its event completes.

3. stop() handles only the waiter's own queue and poller.

   close() (server shutdown) calls stop() before it releases the cache
   contexts. The server's shutdown does not wait for its handlers: the
   transport shuts the affinity pool down with wait=False, and then
   engine.close() closes the modules. stop() instead also failed the
   transfers it had handed to an affinity worker, and waited up to 10 s
   for the running ones before it returned anyway. Now stop() fails only
   the transfers still waiting for their event in its queue, which the
   stopped poller would never run, and stops the poller. A transfer
   already handed to its affinity worker, or running, is left to that
   worker, as without the option; so is an inline transfer whose event
   has completed. The 60 s timeout for a producer event that never
   completes is unchanged.

Tests: a registration made right after a missing-entry lookup is not
used (STORE and RETRIEVE); a re-registration before an inline run drops
the transfer; unregistering frees the entry of a waiting transfer (STORE
and RETRIEVE); stop() neither waits for a running transfer nor fails one
handed to its worker; after stop(), an inline transfer runs if its event
completed and fails if not.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

* [MP] --rocm-host-event-wait: stop() fails hand-offs that have not started

The server shuts down in two steps: server.close() queues the affinity
pool's shutdown sentinel, then engine.close() closes the modules, which
stops the waiter. The poller still runs until stop(): a transfer whose
event completes in between is handed to its affinity worker behind the
sentinel, the worker exits first, and the transfer's response was never
settled.

The poller now records a hand-off until the worker starts it, and stop()
fails the hand-offs that have not started along with the transfers still
waiting for their event. Whichever of the worker and stop() takes a
hand-off first settles it. A running transfer is still left to its
worker.

Tests: a hand-off queued after the worker shutdown sentinel is failed by
stop(); so is one queued behind a busy worker.

Signed-off-by: Lin Sun <lin.sun@amd.com>

commits.author: Daegyu Han
commits.message:
[Bugfix][MP] Stage prefetch keys that land in L1 during the L2 lookup (#6392)

* [Bugfix][MP] Stage prefetch keys that land in L1 during the L2 lookup

A key another request's load admits to L1 between this request's L1
lock pass and its reserve_write made the reservation fail with
KEY_NOT_WRITABLE. The cell was reported as l1_contended, and under the
prefix policy the hit stopped before it, turning a resident chunk into a
miss that the engine recomputed.

reserve_write gains allow_resident: when set, a key that is already
resident is staged like any other. Admission already handles that case
(finish_write_and_reserve_read discards the staging buffer and read-locks
the resident object), so the prefetch controller's state machine is
unchanged. The controller passes the flag only for an L1 the request may
read: the lock pass covers only those, so a resident key there landed
during the lookup. In an affinity L1 excluded by allowed_l1_memory_tags a
resident key stays a miss, as before, and is what l1_contended now
reports. The cost is one redundant L2 load of the landed key, which two
overlapping loads already pay when both reserve before either lands.
Other writers keep the default, so engine stores still de-duplicate on
KEY_NOT_WRITABLE. ShadowL1Manager already stages resident keys.

The two tests that pinned the old drop now expect every key served under
both the prefix and full policies, and fail without the controller
change. An L1 interface test covers the flag and the admission of a
resident key. Docs, the metric description and the P2P skill references
now describe l1_contended by its new meaning.

Signed-off-by: Daegyu Han <hdg9400@gmail.com>

* [Bugfix][MP] Address review: keyword-only allow_resident, document the remaining misses

- allow_resident is keyword-only on L1ManagerInterface, BaseL1Manager
  and ShadowL1Manager, so call sites read as intended.
- staging-and-write-tags.md: a landed key is still a miss when the second
  buffer cannot be allocated (l1_oom) or the redundant load fails.
- prefetch_controller.md: the NO_LOCK limitation (a request can be served
  a temporary resident object that is freed when its last reader releases
  it) moves from the PR description into the limitations list, and the
  TestReservationFailures bullet now says a key landed after the lock pass
  is served.
